method_description: gate kernel: care-set gate replacement moves with annealing, under caps on (A, AD, GD)

campaign.name: 2026-11-16-invsbox
campaign.stopped_by: the user, before the planned 12 hours
campaign.launch: ../_runtime/bin/launch.sh <campaign archive>/run inv 43200 1800 1 (planned 12 h; hub on CPUs 2-11, 10 workers; one conjugation job runner on each of CPUs 12-19; xsrun is the local systemd-run wrapper that pins the CPUs and caps memory)
campaign.seed_list: ../_runtime/run/seeds.list (the 91 pinned NIST inverse circuits, written by mkqueue.py)
campaign.hub_command: cd <checkout> && XS_INVSBOX=1 XS_INVSBOX_LINE=1 PYTHONPATH=<campaign archive>/shim python3 search/nonlinear/boolflux/hub/scheduler.py --dir <campaign archive>/run/hub --cpus 2-11 --hours 11.9333 --seed-list <campaign archive>/run/seeds.list --ops polish,pull,join,trb --seconds polish=90,pull=90,join=60,trb=30 --eps 0.25 --seed 1

runtime_layer.note: the inverse S-box support the run used, outside the repository at c0fb67d (BoolFlux was forward-only there): the shim rebinds, in-process, the S-box tables of boolflux/targets.py and independent/verify.py to their inverse tables and the NIST comparison set to the 91 inverse circuits; invconjpull.py runs ops/conjpull.py with inverse conjugates. Inverse support is being added to the BoolFlux code itself
